words.gloss: he who desires / is infatuated with

literal: Without considering (his duty), the wealth of him who desires a woman will bring shame as a great shame.
translation: The prosperity of a man who, disregarding his own duty, is infatuated with his wife, will only bring him a great and humiliating shame.
modern: தன் கடமையை மதிக்காமல், தன் மனைவியின் விருப்பத்தையே விரும்பி நடப்பவனுடைய செல்வமும் பெருமையும், அவனுக்குப் பெரிய அவமானத்தையே தரும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against losing one's self-respect and sense of duty by being overly submissive to one's wife. The word 'pēṇātu' means not cherishing or neglecting one's duties and self-respect. When a man is infatuated ('viḻaivāṉ') with a woman to the point of neglecting his responsibilities, any wealth or status ('ākkam') he possesses will not bring him honor. Instead, it will only result in a great, public disgrace ('nāṇāka nāṇu tarum') that makes him a laughingstock.
